final_answer:
Let \(\eta\in\mathbb F_p^\times\) be a fixed nonsquare.

For any embedded field \(E\simeq \mathbb F_{p^2}\) in \(M_{1024}(\mathbb F_p)\), the \(1024\)-dimensional module is \(512\) copies of the natural \(2\)-dimensional \(\mathbb F_p\)-module for \(\mathbb F_{p^2}\). Hence for \(\alpha\in E\),
\[
\operatorname{tr}_{M_{1024}}(\alpha)=512\,\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathbb F_{p^2}/\mathbb F_p}(\alpha).
\]
Since \(p\) is odd, \(512\neq 0\) in \(\mathbb F_p\). Thus the trace-zero elements of \(E\) form a one-dimensional \(\mathbb F_p\)-space, generated by some \(X\) with
\[
X^2=\lambda I
\]
for a nonsquare \(\lambda\). For each field \(E\), there are exactly two trace-zero generators \(X\in E\) satisfying \(X^2=\eta I\).

So it suffices to count ordered tuples \((X_v)\) with
\[
X_v^2=\eta I,
\]
and
\[
X_vX_w=-X_wX_v
\]
exactly for incident point-line pairs, while all other distinct pairs commute. The desired number of field families is then this count divided by \(2^{30}\), because \(W(3,2)\) has \(15+15=30\) vertices.

Let \(N\) be the \(15\times 15\) point-line incidence matrix over \(\mathbb F_2\). The commutation form on the \(30\) generators has block matrix
\[
B=\begin{pmatrix}0&N\\ N^T&0\end{pmatrix}.
\]
We need \(\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb F_2}N\).

The orthogonal complement of the column space of \(N\) consists of functions \(f:V\setminus\{0\}\to\mathbb F_2\) satisfying
\[
f(x)+f(y)+f(x+y)=0
\]
whenever \(\langle x,y\rangle=0\). These are exactly the functions
\[
f(x)=\ell(x)
\quad\text{or}\quad
f(x)=q(x)+\ell(x),
\]
where \(\ell\) is linear and
\[
q(x)=x_1x_2+x_3x_4.
\]
Thus this space has dimension \(5\), so
\[
\operatorname{rank}N=15-5=10.
\]
Therefore
\[
\operatorname{rank}B=20,
\qquad
\dim\operatorname{rad}B=30-20=10.
\]

Now form the algebra generated by symbols \(e_v\) with
\[
e_v^2=\eta,\qquad e_ve_w=(-1)^{B(v,w)}e_we_v.
\]
Its radical gives \(10\) independent central signs. Every radical monomial has even weight, so its square is a square in \(\mathbb F_p\). Hence there are
\[
2^{10}
\]
possible central characters. For each central character, the quotient algebra has nondegenerate commutation form of rank \(20\), hence is a central simple algebra of dimension \(2^{20}\). Over the finite field \(\mathbb F_p\), every central simple algebra splits, so each quotient is
\[
M_{2^{10}}(\mathbb F_p)=M_{1024}(\mathbb F_p).
\]

For each of the \(2^{10}\) irreducible representations, conjugation by \(\mathrm{GL}_{1024}(\mathbb F_p)\) gives
\[
\frac{G}{p-1}
\]
distinct ordered matrix tuples, since the centralizer is exactly the scalar matrices. Thus the number of ordered generator tuples is
\[
2^{10}\frac{G}{p-1}.
\]

Dividing by \(2^{30}\) to pass from generators to fields gives
\[
\boxed{\frac{G}{2^{20}(p-1)}}.
\]
